paper.title_en: Traversable wormholes from galactic dark matter halos in <math altimg="si45.svg" display="inline" id="d1e551"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> gravity
paper.abstract_en: In this work, we investigate the existence of traversable wormhole solutions within <math altimg="si45.svg" display="inline" id="d1e727"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> gravity by assuming higher-order curvature model <math altimg="si143.svg" display="inline" id="d1e740"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mi>R</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mo><mi>α</mi><msup><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>γ</mi><mi>R</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>. The investigation is performed using three well-established galactic dark matter halo profiles: the Universal Rotation Curve (URC), Navarro-Frenk-White (NFW) model-I, and NFW model-II. By solving the modified field equations, we establish that these dark matter distributions are capable of generating physically acceptable wormhole shape functions that satisfy the wormhole geometries (e.g. flare-out condition at the throat) for appropriate choices of the model parameters. Additionally, we investigate the associated effective energy conditions, obtained from the total (matter plus curvature-induced) stress–energy content of the modified field equations, and show that the effective null energy condition (NEC) is violated in the vicinity of the throat. This violation is a generic geometric requirement of the flare-out condition at a traversable wormhole throat and is not, by itself, a statement about dynamical stability, which is not addressed in the present work. Our findings suggest that, within the context of non-linear <math altimg="si45.svg" display="inline" id="d1e781"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> gravity, realistic galactic dark matter halos can act as effective sources for sustaining wormhole geometries. This establishes a potential link between dark matter phenomenology and higher-order curvature corrections in gravitational theory.
